rounds.text: CHD Chemicals Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation of 0.63x price-to-book on a book value of ₹ 12.7 [E1], significantly below the sector benchmark P/B of 1.76x [E6]. Operational momentum is turning positive with a notable quarterly operating margin of 12% in Sep 2026 compared to 0% in the year-ago quarter [E27]. The company is actively strengthening its balance sheet by reducing its borrowings to Rs 4.68 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 5.77 Cr a year earlier [E34]. Furthermore, the business is generating positive cash, delivering Rs 0.76 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 0.63 Cr in free cash flow as of Mar 2026 [E31, E32]. Profit growth is exceptionally strong, featuring a compounded profit growth of 93% over the trailing twelve months [E17] and net profit surging 460% year-over-year [E53], outperforming recent 1-year price growth by 49% [E40]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor compounded sales growth of -40% over the past five years and carries low historical returns on equity [E14, E23, E45].

The company suffers from severe and persistent long-term top-line contraction, delivering a compounded sales growth of -18% over 10 years, -40% over 5 years, and -35% over 3 years [E13, E14, E15, E45]. Profitability metrics are deeply depressed, reflected in a negative return on equity of -2.5% [E12] and a median return on equity of -1% over 3 years [E24], alongside a trailing twelve-month operating margin of -0% [E26]. Fundamental solvency and efficiency indicators flag severe distress, including a low interest coverage ratio [E44], a potential capitalization of interest costs [E48], and an extraordinarily bloated debtor collection period of 1,091 days [E49]. Furthermore, the valuation is heavily disconnected from its fundamental earning power, carrying an EV/EBITDA of 56.24x that towers far above the sector benchmark of 10.54x [E10], while promoter ownership remains low at just 27.5% [E46]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated recent positive operating and free cash flows of Rs 0.76 Cr and Rs 0.63 Cr respectively for Mar 2026 [E31, E32], alongside a notable quarter of margin expansion [E27].

Conceded: long-term sales growth has indeed contracted over 10, 5, and 3 years [E13, E14, E15, E45], and ROE sits at -2.5% [E12]. However, the bear's focus on historical contraction ignores an ongoing structural turnaround, evidenced by recent TTM sales growth of 10% [E16] and a dramatic 93% surge in TTM profit growth [E17]. The bear attacks low promoter holding [E46], yet insider-bias checks warn against dismissing a turnaround on stale sentiment when results score 100/100 and net profit jumps 460% YoY [E56]. Furthermore, debt has been actively reduced to Rs 4.68 Cr from Rs 5.77 Cr [E34], proving management is deleveraging despite the bear's solvency concerns. The bear highlights bloated debtor days [E49] and weak interest coverage [E44], but glosses over the tangible reality of positive operating cash flow of Rs 0.76 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 0.63 Cr as of March 2026 [E31, E32]. Finally, while the bear fixates on high EV/EBITDA [E10], it completely overlooks that the stock trades at an attractive P/B of 0.63x—well below the sector benchmark of 1.76x [E6]—offering deep asset backing for a company actively expanding its quarterly operating margin to 12% in September 2026 [E27].

Conceded: operating cash flow is positive at Rs 0.76 Cr and free cash flow stands at Rs 0.63 Cr for March 2026 [E31, E32]. However, the bull's framing of a structural turnaround ignores the multi-year evidence of sustained top-line decay, including a 10-year contraction of -18%, a 5-year drop of -40%, and a 3-year decline of -35% [E13, E14, E15, E45]. The reliance on a single quarter's 12% operating margin in September 2026 [E27] glosses over the official designation of the yearly and quarterly trends as inconsistent [E28, E29]. While the bull dismisses promoter concerns, insider skin in the game remains low at 27.49% [E36, E46]. Furthermore, the valuation argument citing a P/B of 0.63x [E6] ignores critical red flags indicating that the company suffers from low interest coverage, negative return on equity of -2.5%, and alarming debtor days stretching to 1,091 days alongside the risk of capitalized interest costs [E12, E44, E48, E49].
